newsitem.title: UK: Clean tankers revive, higher rates may continue.
newsitem.headline: Clean tankers revive, higher rates may continue.

text.p: The clean tanker market revived this week as arbitrage windows opened up, with signs that the gains may continue, brokers said on Friday.

"Freight rates for clean vessels are showing a slow rejuvenation after the depression which followed the euphoria and excitement of rate levels and enquiry at the turn of the year, and owners are now looking forward with every expectation to these improvements being sustained," said brokers E.A. Gibson in their weekly tanker report.
Cross-Mediterranean 27,500 tonne naphtha cargoes reached at least as high as W270, with gas oil at W210/215 ex-Skikda and there was also good interest in moving both products to Japan, brokers said.
The Caribbean market firmed to at least W300 as the result of a sudden rush to secure Boston-beam vessels early in the week, Gibson said.
Long-range rates were generally flat, with owners eyeing the Med rather than the Middle East, but Mideast/Japan 55,000 tonne cargoes continued to command W200, they added.

The transatlantic market was firm with W190 paid for 60,000 tonnes, and enquiry rose in inter-U.K./Cont over the week with 25,000 tonnes of gas oil Ventspils/NWE fetching W210 for first half March. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
